notes:
VERDICT: DRIFT. 1/1 attempts succeeded on the first try (0 failures, well under the 3-attempt cap). No error was provoked in this probe, so the family's known bare-{success:false} error-envelope defect (10 prior confirmed hits) was not exercised here — nothing to add to that count from this run.

**PUT-VS-PATCH, and the linked defect specifically — PATCH semantics confirmed, no data loss.** The update sent only `elapsed_time` (45 -> 90); `status`, `content` and `defects` were all omitted from the request body. The read-back (both the update's own 200 response and a subsequent independent get_exploratory_session read) shows: `status` unchanged ('note'), `content` byte-identical, and — the field this probe specifically targeted — the linked defect TM-1234 (defect record id 849732) survived completely intact, with its own id and created_at unchanged. This is genuine partial-update (PATCH) behavior for the fields not included in the request, and it matches the capability's own declared guidance ('omit the key to leave [defects] alone'). It does NOT reproduce the sibling defect on update_shared_step (silently recreating a row under a new id when resent without its id, orphaning references): log 544 kept the same id (544) under the same session_id (779), and defect record 849732 kept its own id unchanged — no recreate, no orphaning, no silent drop. Net: this specific data-loss shape was hunted for and NOT found — the linked defect survives an unrelated single-field update.

**Derived field, demonstrated (not just observed).** The prior get_exploratory_session probe on session 779 noted `actual_duration: 165` while the session was active and never closed, exactly equal to the sum of its two logs' elapsed_time (120 + 45), and flagged this as an observed pattern rather than a proven mechanism. This probe changed log 544's elapsed_time from 45 to 90 (delta +45) and re-read the session: `actual_duration` came back **210** — exactly 120 + 90, i.e. it moved by precisely the same +45 delta as the log-level change. session_state stayed 'active' and closed_at stayed null throughout. This converts the earlier note into a demonstrated mechanism: actual_duration is not a value set on close as its own declared description claims — it is live-recomputed as the sum of the session's log elapsed_time values on every read of the session, independent of session_state.

**session_log_count stayed correct.** Read back at 2 after the update (which changed an existing log's field, not the log count) — no count-vs-rows drift observed on this call, not a 6th hit for the family's count-vs-rows pattern (5 confirmed elsewhere).

**Inherited drift from create_exploratory_session_log, confirmed present on update too.** All four items named in the brief reproduce on this endpoint's own 200 response: (1) `session_log.hashed_id` is named in the returns summary but is absent both from the response and from describeCapability's own expanded 200 properties block — the declaration disagrees with itself before any live comparison. (2) `session_log.project_id` and `session_log.group_id` are returned (379335744, 3452) but undeclared anywhere. (3) `defects[].id` (849732) and `defects[].created_at` are returned though the declared defects item schema only has `issue_id`/`issue_type`. (4) `attachment_relations` is named in the `returns` summary but missing from the expanded 200 `properties` block; the live response includes it (`[]`), so the response matches the summary and exposes the summary/properties-block disagreement rather than resolving it. None of this is new relative to the create path — it is the same drift, now confirmed to persist through an update call rather than being create-specific.
